column1: # Constellation Lexical Bridge — seed v1 (M10).
# This is a tiny hand-picked seed used to exercise the lexicon architecture
# end-to-end until M11 ships the 20K-concept core tier. The format below
# scales to that milestone unchanged — M11 simply adds more rows (and may
# switch the packaging to a pre-compiled binary blob at `lexicon_v*.bin`,
# but the seed will remain parseable for regression use).
# Format per row (TAB-separated):
#   concept_id<TAB>pos<TAB>lang:lemma,lemma,...<TAB>lang:lemma,lemma,...<TAB>...
# - `concept_id` is a stable slug like `c:book`. Grep-friendly across the
#   dataset; does not change once published.
# - `pos` is one of the `arabic::PartOfSpeech` variants: Noun / Verb /
#   Adjective / Adverb / ProperNoun / Particle / Foreign / Unknown. Empty
#   string (two consecutive tabs) means Unknown.
# - Each subsequent column is `lang_code:lemma1,lemma2,...`. Lang codes
#   are the ISO-639-1 codes that round-trip with `arabic::Lang::code`:
#   ar, de, en, es, fa, fr, he, hi, ja, ko, pt, ru, tr, ur, zh. Unknown
#   codes are skipped with a debug warning.
# - Arabic lemmas are stored unvocalized (no diacritics / tashkeel /
#   tatweel). The lookup normalizes both the seed at build-time and the
#   caller's query at read-time so `كِتَاب` still finds `كتاب`.
# - Blank lines and lines beginning with `#` are ignored.
# - Columns may appear in any order; the parser keys by `lang_code:`.
# - Rows are accepted in any order; the builder sorts before FST
#   compilation so the resulting graph is deterministic.
